localChanges: A computer player that has no city by its fifth turn now founds one where its Settlers stand, so no civilization sits out the game on a bad start (#207).

Computer players no longer build nothing but soldiers once they have met an enemy. Each city keeps the defenders it needs, builds attackers and explorers in proportion to the empire's size, and then builds improvements and Wonders, one Wonder at a time in the most productive city (#206).
Coastal cities build a Trireme once Map Making is known, and it explores the sea while keeping to the coast, so it isn't lost (#208).

log: A new generic strategy, FoundCapital, runs ahead of WorkerTurn. From turn 5 (a constructor parameter), a worker of a player with no city founds one where it stands, whether or not the tile passes shouldBuildCity. Before then, and once the player has a city, it does nothing and WorkerTurn looks for a good site as before.

On seed 3 the Zulu start on a one-tile island whose only tile scores 158 against shouldBuildCity's 160, so their Settlers never moved or founded a city (civ-clone/web-renderer#207). They now found it on turn 5. Every other first city in 40 arena games was founded by turn 5, so the rule changes nothing else.
The capture test removes the Settlers that building its world spawns, which would otherwise found a city and draw the Warrior back to defend it.

City production (lib/Civ1/buildItemInCity.ts) now builds each kind of unit only while the player has fewer than it wants, and otherwise falls through to Wonders and improvements (civ-clone/web-renderer#206):

Defenders: while a city has fewer units that can defend it than defendersWanted (lib/City/defence.ts), which Garrison now shares. Production wanted two units on the tile while Garrison kept one in a city under size 6, so the second walked off and the city built another: 436 of 480 choices in six games were that defender.

Explorers, new, ahead of Settlers: the cheapest land unit that can fight, while there is land to explore and fewer than 3 + 2 per city are out. The defender churn was what explored the map, and without this, explored tiles fall by 40-60%.
Attackers: while there is something to attack and fewer than 1 per city, rather than whenever an enemy city is known.
Wonders: one at a time, in the player's most productive city. The old test wanted a single Production yield over 4, but a city's yields come one per tile and unit, so it was almost never true.
The random pick no longer includes ships, which were lost at sea.
The numbers come from ProductionPolicy, which ChooseProduction asks for per player (civ-clone/web-renderer#157 can derive it from the leader's traits).
From review of the previous commit:
The attacker and explorer quotas count units the player's cities are building as well as those it has, so cities choosing in the same turn don't all build the last one wanted.

The attacker branch builds only a land unit whose attack beats its defence (the same test the quota counts by), and is skipped when there is none. With only Warriors to build, contact made every city build Warriors that never counted towards the quota.
Garrison counts the defenders on the tile (isDefender, shared with production), not every unit, so Settlers in a small city no longer stop its only Warrior from fortifying.

BuildExplorerShip, a new generic strategy ahead of ChooseProduction, builds the cheapest ship a city can when the player has more than one city, no ship and none on order, the city has its defenders, and the water beside it reaches sea the player hasn't explored (lib/City/explorerShip.ts). With Civ1's units that is a Trireme once Map Making is known (civ-clone/web-renderer#208).

Civ1's canReturnAfter now keeps a Trireme safe (lib/Civ1/trireme.ts): it moves off the coast, or attacks from there, only with a move to spare and a coastal tile beside it, so it never ends its moves off the coast, where civ1-unit loses it half the time.
Missions: exploring the sea now comes before hunting enemy units, as exploring land already did. Ahead of it, the new Triremes went after enemy ships and were sunk.

A mission skips any target the unit can't reach by land (or by sea, for a ship) before searching for a path to it (lib/Unit/reachable.ts). Once ships show the coasts of other continents, every land unit looking for a mission searched its whole continent for each of those tiles, and some games took ten times as long. Play is unchanged: the checksums of seeds 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 are identical with and without it.
Transports and escorts to other continents aren't part of this.

From review: every known water tile beside an unknown one is a sea tile to explore, so a lake whose far shore the player hadn't seen passed the check, and a city on it could build a Trireme that could never leave. isOnSea now also wants the city's body of water to be at least 20 tiles, judged from the map, as Civ1's own AI knows the extent of each ocean. No lake arises in the 40 arena games: the numbers are unchanged.
